behavior: Outbound bridge Deliver requests for Ready and Input alerts carry only the fixed title, a subtitle from manual_title or the session name, and a project/workspace/name(#id) body; generated conversation titles, labels, invocation ids, turn ids, paths and bidi controls are excluded, and identity text is clipped to 80 characters with byte caps.

signal_reason: Positive assertions pin title, navigation validity, session id and the exact body, plus 80-char and byte caps, and negative scans reject PRIVATE_GENERATED, PRIVATE_LABEL, PRIVATE_CONVERSATION, PRIVATE_INVOCATION, /private/path and turn- in the outbound file (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/desktop.rs:3610-3650).

recommendation_reason: Grounded, decisive privacy assertions with no equivalent named coverage; cost is modest and does not affect value.
cost_drivers: fake bridge shell client spawned per outbound operation
wait_bridge polling with a 3 s deadline

behavior: After the automatic poll budget expires for a permission-pending bridge, repeated emit passes issue no additional Status or Authorize requests; an explicit O check on NotDetermined issues exactly one Status, marks permission unconfirmed, and q still detaches.
failure_caught: Expiry restarting automatic polling or re-issuing Authorize after permission became NotDetermined, which would storm the user with authorization requests.

uniqueness_reason: Distinct from the expired-permission matrix: this row covers the automatic poll budget for PermissionPending without an expired manual check.
fidelity_reason: Uses the real bridge control state machine and emit loop against a fake client status file; the fake is appropriate because the subject is the polling policy, not the native prompt.
recommendation_reason: Grounded bounded-poll policy check with a decisive negative assertion; no equivalent body in the shard.
cost_drivers: wait_bridge polling with a 3 s deadline

behavior: For each of available, denied, not_determined and permission_pending replies after an expired authorization, only an explicit O Status check recovers: the palette names the real action, the checking notice clears on completion, bindings change with the resulting status, and disabling desktop notifications permits no recovery traffic.

behavior: Six malformed, incompatible or failing client replies map to Failed or Incompatible with fixed restart guidance that never echoes host error text and offers no recovery control; a missing client maps to the NotInstalled guidance.

behavior: An incompatible bridge reply triggers --check-contract with the schema and wire versions; exit 0 yields the older-running-build restart offer, exit 78 yields the needs-updating repair offer, and the checked arguments are recorded.
failure_caught: Both stale-app and stale-process incompatibilities collapsing to one banner, so the user is told to restart when the app needs updating, or --check-contract being called with the wrong contract versions.

behavior: For an invalid-sound-status reply, invalid JSON and a nonzero exit, run_bridge returns Failed and, after the client has already been reaped, does not SIGKILL the former process group: a directly owned witness that joined that group survives and exits cleanly with no signal.
failure_caught: run_bridge killing a reaped client's former PID or process group, which can hit an unrelated process that reused the group after the client exited, possibly destroying someone else's work.
criticality_reason: A stale process-group SIGKILL is a wrong-target destructive action against unrelated processes (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/desktop.rs:1330-1349); this is the only protection for that reap-versus-signal ordering.
signal_reason: Asserts the witness joined the client group, the client reached its expected exit, and that the witness survived with exit code 0 and signal None for three failure shapes (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/desktop.rs:4203-4363).
uniqueness_reason: Unique failure mode: no other reviewed test covers signalling after reaping. The FIFO gate makes the reap-before-cleanup ordering observable rather than assumed.
fidelity_reason: The process-group ownership and reaping behaviour is the subject, and the test uses real spawned processes, a real FIFO gate, getpgid and libc signal checks, so the OS boundary is genuine even though the client is a shell script.
recommendation_reason: Decisive, unique protection for a destructive wrong-target signal; keep regardless of cost.
cost_drivers: spawned witness in the client process group
thread::scope plus poll loops with HOST_TIMEOUT

behavior: An endless-output client returns Failed within the host timeout; emit_desktop_notifications returns without blocking on a sleeping client; dropping the Dashboard returns quickly and leaves a separately owned persistent host process alive.
failure_caught: Unbounded client stdout or a blocking bridge call wedging the Dashboard, or Dashboard teardown killing a persistent host it does not own.
criticality_reason: Bounded output protects memory and a non-blocking emit protects the whole dashboard workflow; teardown killing the persistent app would be a wrong-target action (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/desktop.rs:1183-1350).
signal_reason: Asserts Failed status, elapsed bounds for run_bridge and emit, detach returning under a second, and that the persistent sleep process is still alive (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/desktop.rs:4370-4416).
uniqueness_reason: Distinct from the reaped-failure test: here the claims are output bounding, non-blocking emit and ownership-preserving drop.
fidelity_reason: Real /usr/bin/yes output flood, a real /bin/sleep process in its own group and a real fake client; timing is an observed mechanism, not a measured flake cause.
recommendation_reason: Grounded bounded-output and ownership checks on real processes; unique in reviewed coverage.
cost_drivers: timing bounds around emit and drop

behavior: After enabling ready sound, Enter moves the Dashboard into Terminal mode and the S keystroke is sent as a PTY byte instead of toggling the setting, which stays enabled.
failure_caught: The S ready-sound binding still matching in Terminal mode and swallowing a keystroke meant for the agent PTY.

signal_reason: Asserts Enter enters Terminal mode, the exact PTY bytes b"S", and that the setting is unchanged (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/desktop.rs:4422-4448).
uniqueness_reason: Same contract as the desktop-notification toggle test for a different key and setting; the negative case protects the same mode boundary, so the distinction is small but real.
fidelity_reason: Runs the production key dispatch and PTY byte path through Dashboard and real server responses, not a stand-in.
recommendation_reason: Grounded mode-boundary check; its sibling covers a different key, so neither subsumes the other.

behavior: After Ctrl starts a sidebar jump labelled for the target session, a production view_request with changed geometry clears the jump label, so the held modifier can no longer address a stale row index.
failure_caught: A held Ctrl jump continuing to address stale session indexes after the layout changed, so the next digit activates the wrong row.
criticality_reason: A stale jump selects a different session than the user aimed at (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:1648-1670), a bounded navigation failure that does not change durable state.
signal_reason: Asserts the label exists before and is None after view_request at a different size (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:919-943); the boundary is the same shared function the event loop uses.
uniqueness_reason: Only reviewed test for jump-hold cancellation on geometry change; neighbouring attention tests cover jump ordering, not cancellation.
fidelity_reason: Uses the real Dashboard view_request and sidebar_jump state; the direct call is the production boundary described in the comment.
recommendation_reason: Grounded at the production geometry boundary; no equivalent coverage.
cost_drivers: calls view_request directly at a second size

behavior: A public ':' key press queues exactly one Request::Inspect through the outbox, and a second drain returns nothing.
failure_caught: The palette key emitting duplicate Inspect frames or dropping the Inspect request from the outbox.
criticality_reason: A duplicated or missing Inspect suggestion is a minor palette consequence (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/palette.rs:1752-1773) with no durable-state impact.
signal_reason: Asserts one request and its exact kind, then an empty second drain (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:954-968).
uniqueness_reason: Same outbox contract as the dispatch-ordering test, which also asserts Inspect, but this row isolates the single-request property.
fidelity_reason: Drives the real event_action and drain_outbox path without a terminal, which is the production request queue.
recommendation_reason: Grounded single-publish assertion; cheap and distinct enough to retain.

behavior: Dispatching ':' with a held mouse press and a due history page writes AssignedHumanInput cleanup with the captured control epoch, view revision and SGR release bytes, then the due HistoryPage, then Inspect, each with distinct request ids and nothing left queued.
failure_caught: The mouse-release cleanup or the due history page being dropped or reordered behind the Inspect request, leaving a stuck press gesture or stalled history.
criticality_reason: Ordering protects a stuck mouse gesture and an overdue history page (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:419-432) while opening the palette, a bounded interaction failure.
signal_reason: Reads three frames and pins their exact requests, matching control epoch and view revision for the cleanup, plus distinct ids and an empty peer afterwards (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:974-1028).

fidelity_reason: Uses the real dispatch_dashboard_event, flush and socket writer with a real UnixStream pair and fixed viewport terminal.
recommendation_reason: Grounded ordering assertions at the dispatch boundary; complements the mouse-cleanup tests.
cost_drivers: fixed-viewport Terminal over a byte buffer

behavior: A response for an ignored request id writes nothing, and a later quota event flushes the queued SetView followed by the due HistoryPage, then nothing more.
failure_caught: A queued view suppressing the due history page, or an ignored response id emitting a frame on the socket.
criticality_reason: Wrong ordering delays a history page the user is waiting for (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:387-418), a bounded responsiveness failure.

recommendation_reason: Grounded ignored-response and due-history ordering; small but not subsumed.

behavior: Releasing the Ctrl jump before the SetView acknowledgement keeps mode Browse through the bounded input drain; all pre-ack paste and key events up to DASHBOARD_INPUT_BATCH_LIMIT+3 produce no socket frame, and a key after the quiet boundary reaches the destination session.
failure_caught: Keystrokes queued during a jump landing in the destination session's PTY, that is, input issued to a session the user had not yet acknowledged.
criticality_reason: Cross-session input leakage runs typed text or Ctrl-C into the wrong agent (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:469-545), which is wrong ownership of live terminal input.
signal_reason: Asserts mode stays Browse for every InputPending boundary, the peer receives no frame during the drain, focus is the destination only after cutover, and fresh input then arrives (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:1069-1206).

fidelity_reason: Drives the real drain_dashboard_input_then_emit_with loop, dispatch and socket send with a real pair and a controlled event queue.
recommendation_reason: Grounded at the real input boundary with a decisive no-frame assertion; high value.

behavior: initialize_dashboard sends hello(1), tolerates interleaved QuotaChanged events while waiting, applies the hierarchy, sends geometry(2), then reconcile(3), and the resulting hierarchy and quotas match the server readings.
failure_caught: Startup consuming a quota event as the hello or geometry response, so hierarchy or geometry is never applied before the first frame.
criticality_reason: Startup handshake failure leaves an unusable dashboard session (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:751-812), matching the unusable-terminal class.
signal_reason: Asserts request ids and kinds in order, that pre-response quota events do not disturb the wait, and the final hierarchy and quota snapshot (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:1279-1361).
uniqueness_reason: Unique startup ordering coverage: the error test covers failures, not the success path with interleaved events.
fidelity_reason: Runs the real initialize_dashboard against a scripted peer over a real UnixStream pair, with the server side controlled by the test thread.
recommendation_reason: Grounded handshake ordering with interleaved events; no equivalent coverage.
cost_drivers: 2 s read timeouts on both ends

behavior: For failures on hello(1) and geometry(2), an unrelated response id 42 and a quota event are ignored, and the returned error names both the server message and the failed step.
failure_caught: Startup swallowing a real hello or geometry error, or matching an error by the wrong request id, then continuing with an unusable session.
criticality_reason: A missed startup error is reported to the user instead of being silently absorbed (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:814-838); the dashboard still fails, so the consequence is diagnostic quality rather than data.
signal_reason: Loops over failed_id 1 and 2, injects a decoy response id and a quota event, and asserts the error text contains the server message and the step name (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:1367-1428).
uniqueness_reason: Distinct from the success-path startup test: this row protects request-id matching on the error branch.
fidelity_reason: Real initialize_dashboard and read_initial_response against a scripted peer over a socket pair.
recommendation_reason: Grounded negative startup branch with decoy messages; not subsumed.
cost_drivers: two-iteration loop with a server thread each

behavior: For 0, 2 and DASHBOARD_INPUT_BATCH_LIMIT+3 events queued while an Agent confirmation is Loading, the final Ok keeps Browse through the bounded drain, emits no destination Input, and a post-boundary key is delivered to the new session.
failure_caught: Input typed before the agent confirmation acknowledgement being delivered to the newly focused agent session.
criticality_reason: Pre-cutover keystrokes reaching the new session's PTY are wrong-target terminal input (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:469-545).
signal_reason: Asserts Browse at every InputPending boundary, no readable frame on the peer, that the rejected j cannot navigate, and that post-boundary z produces Input (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:1434-1556).
uniqueness_reason: Same invariant as the jump-release test but a different production trigger and event-count boundary; both are needed to cover their respective acknowledgement paths.
fidelity_reason: Real next_dashboard_messages, drain loop, dispatch and socket send with a real pair and vt100-backed terminal.
recommendation_reason: Grounded three-boundary loop with a decisive no-frame assertion; keep.

behavior: Typing a reply into a presented unread session sends MarkReviewed for the exact displayed observation before the Input bytes, only once; viewing or focusing alone reviews nothing, the rest of the reply is input only, and a newer presented Ready becomes the next reply's target.
failure_caught: Reviewing an unread turn that is not displayed, replaying the review on every keystroke, or ordering Input ahead of MarkReviewed so the reply clears a different observation.
criticality_reason: Unread review drives the typing contract between user and agent (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:4774-4800); reviewing the wrong observation can silently discard a response the user never read.
signal_reason: Asserts no traffic on Enter, the exact MarkReviewed with the presented observation before b"x", input-only continuation, and the newer observation as the next target (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:1562-1673).
uniqueness_reason: Three unread rows cover distinct failure modes; this one covers reply-triggered review and its once and ahead-of-input ordering, which the boundary and failed-draw tests do not.
fidelity_reason: Uses the real Dashboard reply path, draw and socket send with a UnixStream pair; the presented observation is committed by the production draw path.
recommendation_reason: Grounded ordering and identity assertions at the real reply boundary; high value.
cost_drivers: draws through a fixed viewport terminal

behavior: An R queued between a SessionChanged(B) message and the next draw still sends MarkReviewed naming the last drawn observation A; after a successful draw the same action names B.
failure_caught: Reviewing an unread observation that was never drawn, or continuing to review a superseded observation after the new frame was presented.
criticality_reason: Marking an unseen response reviewed loses the user's only signal that an agent needs them (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:4760-4788).
signal_reason: Asserts the hierarchy already holds B, the queued R sends A, then a successful draw makes the next R send B (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:1679-1757).
uniqueness_reason: Distinct boundary: message-before-input ordering at the drain boundary, not the reply path or a failed draw.
fidelity_reason: Real next_dashboard_messages and drain loop with a socket pair, message channel and fixed viewport terminal.
recommendation_reason: Grounded presented-versus-updated ordering; no duplicate.

behavior: No review is possible before the first presentation; a failed draw leaves the prior presented observation; a palette overlay and session selection also cannot review until a successful unobscured presentation.
failure_caught: A failed or obscured frame committing a new unread observation, so R marks a response the user never saw.
criticality_reason: Committing presented state on a failed draw reviews an unseen agent response (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/render.rs:390-410), the same lost-signal class as the other unread rows.
signal_reason: Asserts none before the first draw, the original observation after a forced flush error, Inspect while in the overlay, and none after selection without a draw (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:1763-1844).
uniqueness_reason: Distinct from the ordering and reply rows: this one probes draw failure, overlays and session selection as non-presenting events.
fidelity_reason: Production draw path with a custom writer that fails flush, real commit_presented and key dispatch; the failure is injected at the real terminal boundary.
recommendation_reason: Grounded negative presentation cases unique to this row; keep.

behavior: With Quick open, Ctrl-o, control chords, paste including an OSC52 sequence, mouse and resize produce no socket request and no PTY bytes; Ctrl-c clears only the Quick draft; Enter sends exactly one Create, and the Created receipt yields exactly one Submit with the captured text and no Input or AssignedHumanInput.
failure_caught: A Quick-composer keystroke or paste escaping into the PTY (Ctrl-C interrupting an agent, OSC52 writing the clipboard), or Enter emitting Create plus PTY input.
criticality_reason: Input leaking from the modal into the agent PTY can interrupt or drive a running agent (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:553-608) and inject clipboard controls; that is a wrong action rather than a cosmetic one.
signal_reason: Asserts no readable frame after every editing, mouse and resize event, that Ctrl-c clears only the draft, one Create on Enter, one Submit with the exact text, and no Input or AssignedHumanInput (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:1912-2158).
uniqueness_reason: Complements the real-socket-reader row: this covers the Quick modal's dispatch immunity, while the other covers stream separation and Stop identity.

recommendation_reason: Grounded at the real dispatch boundary with decisive negative assertions; keep.

behavior: With a real reader thread, List, Read, Stop and per-conversation histories stay separated across an A/B switch; operator draft edits and Ctrl-c send nothing until the exact Stop; Stop carries the selected turn identity once; terminal keys reach the focused session's PTY; and model text never emits OSC52.
failure_caught: Two operator histories interleaving into one transcript, Stop targeting the wrong turn, operator and terminal input crossing streams, or model text emitting clipboard control sequences.
criticality_reason: Mixed streams or a mis-targeted Stop can stop the wrong turn or corrupt the conversation view (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/operator.rs:825-830, crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:732-750), a wrong-ownership failure.
signal_reason: Asserts per-conversation Read ids, exact Stop identity, no frames for draft editing, PTY Input for x and Ctrl-c byte 3, both histories rendered distinctly, and absence of the injected OSC52 payload (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:2163-2528).
uniqueness_reason: The only reviewed test that runs the production reader thread and interleaves two live operator conversations with terminal input; neighbouring rows cover either operator requests or terminal input separately.
fidelity_reason: Real read_messages thread, socket pair, vt100 parser and terminal writer; the server side is scripted, which is appropriate for stream separation.
recommendation_reason: Grounded end-to-end stream separation with a real reader; unique and high value.

failure_caught: Instance paths missing from the Events popup, or invented paths shown when the Dashboard was given none.
criticality_reason: Missing diagnostic header lines only reduce readability of the Events popup (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/events.rs:347-362).

criticality_reason: Duplicate or lost event lines misinform diagnostic reading but do not affect durable state or workflows (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/events.rs:101-112).

behavior: The Events filter requires every whitespace-separated word to appear case-insensitively in the component, subject or message, and never matches the raw timestamp.
